name: Emptiness in the Perfection of Wisdom sūtras

definitions.definition: All dharmas — aggregates, elements, links, truths, paths, fruits, buddhahood and nirvāṇa — are empty of own-being, unborn, like illusions and dreams; the bodhisattva does not apprehend even 'bodhisattva' or 'perfection of wisdom'; emptiness is not destruction, and is not itself to be grasped.

relations.note: the sūtras of the 'third turning' re-read emptiness as emptiness of stains only
what depends on conditions is called empty

name: The twenty (sixteen, eighteen) emptinesses

definitions.definition: The Large Perfection of Wisdom's list of emptinesses in which the bodhisattva trains: of the internal, external, both, emptiness itself, the great, the ultimate, the conditioned, the unconditioned, the absolute, the beginningless, non-rejection, essential nature, all dharmas, own-marks, the non-apprehended, the own-being of non-being — commonly 'up to' this sixteenth — then of being, non-being, own-being and other-being (twenty); the Chinese tradition often counts eighteen.

notes: Order and list read in the local Kimura e-text (Pañcaviṃśati I).

name: The Diamond Sūtra's 'A is not A, therefore it is called A'

definitions.definition: The recurring formula of the Vajracchedikā: what the Tathāgata taught as X (merit, buddha-dharmas, the perfection of wisdom, dust, world, the marks, beings, self) is taught as not-X; therefore it is called X — affirming the conventional name while denying the ultimate referent.

relations.note: the name conventionally, its emptiness ultimately

name: The nine similes for the conditioned (Vajracchedikā 32)

definitions.definition: Conditioned things are to be seen as stars, a fault of vision, a lamp, a magical show, dew, a bubble, a dream, lightning and a cloud; Kumārajīva has six: dream, illusion, bubble, shadow, dew, lightning.

name: The middle way as true examination of dharmas (Kāśyapaparivarta, Samādhirāja)

definitions.definition: 'Is' and 'is not', permanent and impermanent, self and no-self are extremes; the middle between them — formless, unshowable, without abode — is the middle way; the wise do not take a stand even in the middle.
Buddha-nature is the middle way (Mahāparinirvāṇa).

relations.note: the early middle way between extremes (U36) extended to all dharmas

definitions.definition: Thirty-odd bodhisattvas each name a pair and its transcendence; Mañjuśrī says non-duality is beyond expression; Vimalakīrti's silence is the entry itself.

name: The two truths (sūtra layer)

definitions.definition: The sūtras distinguish conventional designation from the ultimate that is inexpressible, neither the same as nor different from the formations (Saṃdhinirmocana ch. 2-3); the ultimate is beyond even the Buddha's words (Saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyanirdeśa).

notes: The Madhyamaka systematization belongs to U40.

definitions.definition: Seeing dependent origination is seeing the dharma and the Buddha; outward (seed-sprout) and inward (twelve links) dependent origination is neither eternal nor annihilated (Śālistamba); what arises from conditions is unborn and empty (Anavatapta); the twelve links rest on mind (Daśabhūmika 6).

Emptiness, the signless and the wishless, cultivated by the bodhisattva even in dreams, whose fruit he does not realize before his roots are ripe; in the Lotus's Sanskrit they are the herbs that cure the blind.

name: The four noble truths (Mahāyāna sūtra readings)

definitions.definition: In emptiness there are no suffering, origin, cessation or path (Heart); of the four only cessation is permanent, the one truth and refuge (Śrīmālā).
Stream-enterer to arhat do not think 'I have attained', for nothing is attained (Vajracchedikā 9).

From the arising of the thought of awakening, through the perfections, the grounds and irreversibility, to buddhahood — undertaken for all beings, with the armor of vowing to liberate countless beings who are not found; neither destroying the conditioned nor abiding in the unconditioned.

relations.note: the arhat's path; Mahāyāna sūtras call its nirvāṇa not final

name: The thought of awakening (bodhicitta) in the sūtras

definitions.definition: The resolve for buddhahood for all beings; its nature is luminous, a 'no-thought'; at its first arising perfect awakening is already attained (Avataṃsaka); even the lowest aspirants to Sukhāvatī must arouse it.

notes: Relative and ultimate bodhicitta as a pair is systematized in the śāstras (U40).

definitions.definition: Giving, morality, patience, vigor, meditation and wisdom; wisdom leads the other five, which without it are not even called perfections; giving should be unsupported, patience free of the notion of self.
The six plus skillful means, vow, power and knowledge, one predominating on each of the ten grounds.

name: The ten grounds (bhūmi) of the Daśabhūmika

definitions.definition: Joyful, Stainless, Luminous, Radiant, Hard-to-Conquer, Facing, Far-Going, Immovable, Good Intelligence, Cloud of Dharma — each with its perfection; mind-only realized on the sixth, acceptance of non-arising on the eighth, consecration on the tenth.

name: The signs of the irreversible bodhisattva

definitions.definition: Aṣṭa ch. 17: he does not look to other teachers, has no doubt, keeps the ten wholesome ways even in dreams, is not deceived when Māra in the Buddha's form denies the teaching; ch. 19-20 add dream-signs.

The buddhas' and bodhisattvas' adaptation of teaching and conduct to beings: three vehicles for one, parinirvāṇa displayed by an eternal Buddha, the householder-sage who visits brothels, the conjured city; paired with wisdom as the bodhisattva's two wings.
There is only one buddha-vehicle; the three are its skillful presentations; all who hear the Lotus become buddhas.
The two vehicles enter the great vehicle; the arhat's nirvāṇa is not final (Śrīmālā).
Śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha and bodhisattva vehicles — skillful means (Lotus) or matched to fixed lineages (Laṅkāvatāra, Saṃdhinirmocana).

name: The seven parables of the Lotus

definitions.definition: Burning house (ch. 3), lost son (4), medicinal herbs (5), conjured city (7), jewel in the robe (8), king's topknot jewel (14), physician and his sons (16) — each showing skillful means leading to the one vehicle.

notes: The traditional East Asian count (Vasubandhu's commentary, Tiantai); Kumārajīva chapter numbers.

name: The arhat's nirvāṇa is not final

definitions.definition: The nirvāṇa of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is a conjured resting place; śrāvakas are predicted to buddhahood; one who has entered the disciples' certainty cannot produce bodhicitta (Vimalakīrti).
Arhats still have fear, remaining birth and the ground of ignorance (Śrīmālā).

relations.note: the Pali account treats arahatta as final

definitions.definition: Merit is rejoiced in and turned toward awakening for all, without apprehension of the three spheres — otherwise the dedication is 'poisoned'.
Giving, pleasant speech, beneficial conduct and consistency (acting alike), by which bodhisattvas gather beings; Śrīmālā vows to use them.
The bodhisattva sees beings as reflections and echoes and yet has true love for them — love that is peaceful, non-dual, without grasping — together with compassion, joy and equanimity.

relations.note: the immeasurables of U36 practiced with insight into emptiness

definitions.definition: The bodhisattva is ill because beings are ill, as parents are ill with their only son; the sick bodhisattva sees his illness, and beings', as unreal, and so has compassion free of sentimental views.

name: The passions as the family of the Tathāgata

definitions.definition: The body-view, ignorance, craving, the poisons and the sixty-two views are the Tathāgata's family: as lotuses grow in mud, buddha-qualities grow in beings in the mud of passions, not in those who have entered the unconditioned.

name: Women's bodies and buddhahood in the Mahāyāna sūtras

definitions.definition: The sūtras record both the view that a woman's body cannot attain buddhahood (Śāriputra's objection; the nāga princess transforming into a man; Bhaiṣajyaguru's and Amitābha's vows that women may be freed from the woman's state) and the teaching that all dharmas are neither male nor female (the goddess in Vimalakīrti), together with women teachers (Śrīmālā) and women predicted to buddhahood (the Ganges goddess).
The bodhisattva's liberation in which Sumeru enters a mustard seed and the four oceans a pore without change — a display that shows the non-obstruction of dharmas.

name: Purity of mind, purity of the buddha-field

definitions.definition: As the bodhisattva's mind is purified, so is his buddha-field; the Buddha's field is always pure but appears impure to impure minds.

relations.note: a pure land 'here' vs. pure lands elsewhere; both taught

name: Pure lands and buddha-fields

definitions.definition: Buddha-fields purified by a buddha's vows, in the ten directions: Amitābha's Sukhāvatī in the west, Akṣobhya's Abhirati and Bhaiṣajyaguru's lapis land in the east; born there beings do not retrogress.

notes: Pure Land doctrine and schools: U43.

definitions.definition: Countless world-systems in all directions, each with its buddha; buddhas from them gather and testify; the Lotus-Treasury world-ocean holds them on a lotus.

name: The thousand buddhas of the fortunate aeon

definitions.definition: In this aeon a thousand buddhas appear, Śākyamuni the fourth and Maitreya the fifth.

name: Interpenetration in the Avataṃsaka (sūtra layer)

definitions.definition: Worlds in each atom and pore, the Buddha's body filling the dharmadhātu, Maitreya's tower in which every tower contains all others without obstruction.

notes: Huayan's systematic doctrine (Indra's net, four dharmadhātus) is U54.

name: Sudhana's spiritual friends (Gaṇḍavyūha)

definitions.definition: The good friends Sudhana visits, in the order of Vaidya's sections 3-56; Huayan maps them onto the stages of the path (fifty-three counting Mañjuśrī twice and Samantabhadra).

notes: List read from the section headings of the local Vaidya e-text (sections 3-56).

definitions.definition: The vows of good conduct: homage, offering, confession, rejoicing, requesting teaching, requesting the buddhas to stay, dedication — and, in the 40-fascicle Chinese, ten vows adding following the buddhas, according with beings and universal dedication; recited for rebirth in Sukhāvatī.

name: The sūtra as object of worship

definitions.definition: Writing, honoring, reciting and teaching a sūtra is supreme merit; where it is kept or taught is a caitya without relics, the Tathāgata's whole body.

name: The decline of the dharma (sūtra layer)

definitions.definition: In the 'last five hundred years' of the true dharma's destruction, some will still have faith in and keep these sūtras; the Lotus's peaceful practices are for the latter age.

name: Dhāraṇī and mantra in the sūtras

definitions.definition: Dhāraṇīs protecting the preacher (Lotus 26), the Heart's mantra of the perfection of wisdom, the Śūraṅgama mantra, the six-syllable vidyā of Avalokiteśvara.
Rely on the dharma not the person, the meaning not the letter, definitive not provisional sūtras, gnosis not consciousness; the finger is not the moon.

name: Provisional and definitive meaning

definitions.definition: The Buddhist hermeneutic: the Akṣayamati calls sūtras teaching emptiness definitive and those teaching self and beings provisional; the Saṃdhinirmocana calls the first two turnings provisional and the third definitive.

relations.note: the two sūtras apply the distinction differently

notes: Reconciliation principle P5-neyartha is drawn from these texts.

name: The three turnings of the dharma-wheel

definitions.definition: Saṃdhinirmocana ch. 7: the four truths (first), naturelessness taught in a hidden manner (second), and naturelessness well distinguished (third, definitive).
In Tibetan buddha-nature traditions the tathāgatagarbha sūtras and RGV are counted as the third turning.
The Buddha awakened incalculable aeons ago; his lifespan is immeasurable and his parinirvāṇa a skillful display (Lotus 16; Golden Light 2).
The Tathāgata's body is the permanent vajra body (Mahāparinirvāṇa).
The dharmakāya is beginningless, uncreated, permanent, the cessation of suffering itself; whether or not buddhas appear, the garbha is unchanging.
The Tathāgata's body is the dharmakāya and is not ill (Vimalakīrti 3.44).

name: The bodies of the Buddha (sūtra layer)

definitions.definition: The sūtras distinguish the form-body with its marks, by which the Tathāgata is not truly seen, from the dharma-body; the Lotus's eternal Buddha and his emanations anticipate three bodies.
The RGV: from the dharmakāya arise the enjoyment and emanation bodies for others.

notes: The trikāya doctrine is systematized in Yogācāra (U41).

name: The thirty-two marks of a great man

definitions.definition: The bodily marks of a buddha (and cakravartin); the Tathāgata is not to be seen by them; they belong to the form-bodies as fruits of maturation.
Flesh, divine, wisdom, dharma and buddha eye, all possessed by the Tathāgata.

name: Mind of the three times cannot be got at

definitions.definition: Past, present and future thought cannot be found (Vajracchedikā 18) — a phrase much used in Chan.

name: The four notions (self, being, soul, person)

definitions.definition: Ātma-, sattva-, jīva- and pudgala-saṃjñā, whose presence means one is not a bodhisattva; the buddhas are free of all notions.

name: The dharma as a raft

definitions.definition: Even dharmas are to be abandoned once crossed, still more non-dharmas.

notes: The raft simile is the Pali Alagaddūpama Sutta's (MN 22).

definitions.definition: Mind and giving not resting on any object; the Tathāgata's mind stands nowhere; Kumārajīva's 'produce a mind that abides nowhere'.
No self of persons and no self of dharmas.
Five sense-consciousnesses, mind-consciousness, manas and the ālayavijñāna, from which the others arise like waves; the Saṃdhinirmocana's ādāna/ālaya holds all seeds.
The Laṅkāvatāra identifies the tathāgatagarbha with the ālayavijñāna: it evolves with the seven consciousnesses yet is pure by nature; without it there would be neither saṃsāra nor nirvāṇa.

relations.note: one base seen as defiled (ālaya) and as pure (garbha)

definitions.definition: 'This triple world is mind only' (Daśabhūmika 6); 'all is made by mind' (Avataṃsaka); 'this mind makes the Buddha, this mind is the Buddha' (Contemplation Sūtra); the image in samādhi is cognition only (Saṃdhinirmocana 8); the world is what is seen of one's own mind (Laṅkāvatāra).

name: The four dhyānas of the Laṅkāvatāra

definitions.definition: The dhyāna of the foolish (no-self of persons), of examining meanings (no-self of dharmas), of taking suchness as object, and the Tathāgata's dhyāna.
Sign, name, discrimination, right knowledge and suchness.
Śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha and Tathāgata lineages, the indeterminate and those without lineage (Laṅkāvatāra).
Imagined, dependent and perfected (Saṃdhinirmocana 6; Laṅkāvatāra).
Of characteristic, of arising, and ultimate — the intent behind 'all dharmas lack own-being'.

name: The seven locations of mind refuted (Śūraṅgama)

definitions.definition: Ānanda places the mind inside the body, outside it, hidden in the eye-organ, in darkness and light, where it meets objects, in between, and in non-attachment; each is refuted.

Six objects, six faculties, six consciousnesses and seven elements (including Mahāsthāmaprāpta's recollection of the Buddha and Avalokiteśvara's hearing) by which sages attained penetration; hearing is chosen for this world.

name: The four clear instructions on purity (Śūraṅgama)

definitions.definition: Cutting off lust, killing, stealing and false claims as the foundation of samādhi.

name: The fifty demonic states of the aggregates (Śūraṅgama)

definitions.definition: Ten states for each aggregate that arise in deep meditation; harmless if not taken as sagehood, disastrous if taken so.

All beings have the Tathāgata within, covered by adventitious defilements — the dharmakāya not yet freed; the realm of beings neither increases nor decreases; it is empty of stains and not empty of qualities; all beings, even icchantikas, have it.
The Laṅkāvatāra: taught to remove the fear of no-self, meaning emptiness; the Avataṃsaka: the Tathāgata's wisdom present in all beings.

relations.note: the sūtras call it 'self'; the Laṅkāvatāra says it is not a self
buddha-nature = the emptiness of the highest meaning (Mahāparinirvāṇa); = emptiness (Laṅkāvatāra)

name: The nine similes of the tathāgatagarbha

definitions.definition: Buddha in a withered lotus, honey among bees, kernel in husk, gold in filth, treasure under a poor house, sprout in a fruit, image in rags, king in a poor woman's womb, statue in a clay mould.

name: The three reasons all beings are tathāgatagarbhas (RGV 1.27-28)

definitions.definition: The buddha's knowledge (dharmakāya) pervades beings; suchness is undivided; the buddha-lineage exists in them.

name: The ten aspects of the element (RGV 1.29)

definitions.definition: Essence, cause, fruit, function, endowment, manifestation, states, all-pervasiveness, unchangeability, inseparability.
Buddha, dharma, saṅgha, element, awakening, qualities, activity — the body of the Ratnagotravibhāga.

name: The four perfections of the dharmakāya

definitions.definition: Permanence, bliss, self and purity — the true nature of the Tathāgata's dharmakāya and nirvāṇa, reversing the inverted views about the Tathāgata; cultivated by faith, wisdom, samādhi and compassion.

name: The four inversions and their reversal

definitions.definition: The ordinary inversions take the impermanent as permanent etc.; the śrāvakas' inverted view takes the Tathāgata's permanence, bliss, self and purity as impermanent, suffering, no-self and impure.

name: The garbha empty and not empty

definitions.definition: Empty of the separable defilements; not empty of the inseparable buddha-qualities (Śrīmālā 9; RGV 1.154-155); the Mahāparinirvāṇa's wise see both the empty and the non-empty.

name: Why buddha-nature was taught: the five faults (RGV 1.156-157)

definitions.definition: Discouragement, contempt for inferior beings, grasping the unreal, denying the real, and excessive self-love are removed by the teaching that all beings have buddha-nature.

name: The realm of beings neither increases nor decreases

definitions.definition: Sattvadhātu = tathāgatagarbha = dharmakāya; the one dharmadhātu with three aspects.
The Mahāparinirvāṇa: 'self' means the tathāgatagarbha; no-self is saṃsāra, self is the Tathāgata; the Aṅgulimālīya likewise.
The Laṅkāvatāra denies that the garbha-teaching is the tīrthikas' self.

name: Buddha-nature as the emptiness of the highest meaning and the middle way

definitions.definition: Buddha-nature is paramārtha-śūnyatā, which is wisdom and the middle way (Mahāparinirvāṇa juan 27).

name: The icchantika and the question of universal buddhahood

definitions.definition: The Mahāparinirvāṇa moves from excluding icchantikas to affirming their buddha-nature and refusing a fixed icchantika (four alternatives).
The Laṅkāvatāra: two kinds of icchantika; five lineages including agotra.

Keeping the precepts, no pride, no anger, no envy, no stinginess, giving to the needy, using the four means of attraction, rescuing the suffering, restraining offenders, never forgetting the true dharma.
To gain the knowledge of the true dharma, to teach it, and to protect it at the cost of life.

name: One mind, two aspects (Awakening of Faith)

definitions.definition: Mind as suchness and mind as arising and ceasing; the ālaya where the two combine.
The mind is originally awake; non-awakening depends on it; actualized awakening returns to it (Awakening of Faith); perfect enlightenment is the original mind (Yuanjue jing).

name: Dharmākara's forty-eight vows

definitions.definition: The vows (T360) establishing Sukhāvatī: no evil destinies, golden bodies, superknowledges, infinite light and life, birth for all who call on him (18th), welcome at death (19th), rebirth by dedicating merit (20th).

notes: Detailed doctrine of the vows: U43.

definitions.definition: Beings of the ten directions who sincerely entrust themselves, wish to be born and think of Amitābha even ten times are born there, except those who commit the five grave offences and slander the dharma.

name: The nine grades of birth in Sukhāvatī

definitions.definition: Upper, middle and lower birth, each in three grades (Contemplation Sūtra 14-16), from those with the three minds to the evil-doer saved by ten recitations at death; the Larger Sūtra's three classes of aspirants.
Light, complete faculties, healing, provision, right views, freedom from punishment, food and clothing for all who keep his name.

name: Bodhisattva precepts (sūtra layer)

definitions.definition: The Brahmajāla's ten major and forty-eight minor precepts; the Ākāśagarbha's root downfalls; the Upāsakaśīla's lay precepts.

notes: The Yogācāra vow ritual (Bodhisattvabhūmi) is U41.

definitions.definition: Nine Mahāyāna sūtras venerated as a set by Newar Buddhists: Aṣṭasāhasrikā, Gaṇḍavyūha, Daśabhūmika, Samādhirāja, Laṅkāvatāra, Saddharmapuṇḍarīka, Tathāgataguhya, Lalitavistara, Suvarṇaprabhāsa.
